the bioactivities of naphthazarin and its derivatives are closely related to the reactivity in conjugating glutathione, which is in turn related to the electrophilicity of the quinone moiety.

the cytotoxicity of DMNQ derivatives against L1210 cell line is closely related to their reactivity to form glutathione conjugates, and the inhibition of DNA topo-I is also closely related to their electrophilic reactivity.

the bioactivities of 6-(1-hydroxalkyl)-DMNs are strongly affected by the length of the alkyl chain.
the bioactivities of naphthazarin analogs are closely related to their chemical structure.
the cytotoxicity of DMNQ derivatives is not only dependent on the reactivity in conjugating with glutathione but also on the alkyl chain length of the 1-hydroxy group.
